slides.texte_overlay:
Habits that quietly
rebuild your self-respect
Make your bed every morning. It's a small promise you keep to yourself before anything else. Self-respect is built from promises kept.
Stop talking badly about yourself. "I'm so stupid" becomes "I made a mistake." The way you talk to yourself shapes how you see yourself.
Take care of your body. Train, eat real food, sleep enough. Treating your body well is one of the clearest signs you respect yourself.
Walk away from people who make you feel small. You don't have to argue. Just spend less time with them and more with people who lift you up.
Try this for 30 days: five minutes a day of history, art or science. Becoming a bit wiser every day makes you proud of who you're becoming.
slides.texte_sophia: Try this for 30 days: I do five minutes a day on a micro-learning app like the Sophia app. History, art, science. Becoming a bit wiser every day makes you proud of who you're becoming.

slides.texte_overlay: Finish what you start. A book, a project, a training plan. Every finished thing is proof that you can rely on yourself. Even the small ones count.
Dress well even when nobody sees you. Clean clothes at home, a fresh shirt on a lazy Sunday. You deserve your own effort. It's a habit, not vanity.
